hints: First find the missing probability $\mathrm{P}(6)$ using the fact that all probabilities on the die must sum to 1.
List all pairs of outcomes $(d_1, d_2)$ from two throws that add up to 9.
Calculate the probability of each pair by multiplying the probabilities of the two independent throws, and add the results.
walkthrough:
Find the probability of rolling a $6$ using total probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(6) = 1 - [\mathrm{P}(1) + \mathrm{P}(3) + \mathrm{P}(5)] - [\mathrm{P}(2) + \mathrm{P}(4)]$$
$$\mathrm{P}(6) = 1 - 3(0.1) - 2(0.2) = 1 - 0.3 - 0.4 = 0.3$$

Identify all mutually exclusive pairs of outcomes that sum to $9$:
$$(3, 6), \quad (4, 5), \quad (5, 4), \quad (6, 3)$$

Calculate the probability for each pair using the multiplication rule for independent throws:
$$\mathrm{P}(3, 6) = 0.1 \times 0.3 = 0.03$$
$$\mathrm{P}(4, 5) = 0.2 \times 0.1 = 0.02$$
$$\mathrm{P}(5, 4) = 0.1 \times 0.2 = 0.02$$
$$\mathrm{P}(6, 3) = 0.3 \times 0.1 = 0.03$$

Sum the probabilities of these disjoint outcomes:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{sum} = 9) = 0.03 + 0.02 + 0.02 + 0.03 = 0.10$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the unknown probability $\mathrm{P}(6)$.
The probabilities of all mutually exclusive faces on a die must sum to $1$:
$$\sum_{i=1}^6 \mathrm{P}(i) = 1$$
We are given:
- $\mathrm{P}(1) = \mathrm{P}(3) = \mathrm{P}(5) = 0.1$
- $\mathrm{P}(2) = \mathrm{P}(4) = 0.2$
Therefore:
$$\mathrm{P}(6) = 1 - [0.1 + 0.2 + 0.1 + 0.2 + 0.1] = 1 - 0.7 = 0.3$$

Step 2: List all ordered pairs $(x_1, x_2)$ from two throws that have a sum of $9$:
- $3 + 6 = 9 \implies (3, 6)$
- $4 + 5 = 9 \implies (4, 5)$
- $5 + 4 = 9 \implies (5, 4)$
- $6 + 3 = 9 \implies (6, 3)$
No other pairs of integers between $1$ and $6$ add to $9$.

Step 3: Because consecutive throws are independent, the joint probability of an ordered pair is the product of the individual probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(3, 6) = \mathrm{P}(3) \times \mathrm{P}(6) = 0.1 \times 0.3 = 0.03$$
$$\mathrm{P}(4, 5) = \mathrm{P}(4) \times \mathrm{P}(5) = 0.2 \times 0.1 = 0.02$$
$$\mathrm{P}(5, 4) = \mathrm{P}(5) \times \mathrm{P}(4) = 0.1 \times 0.2 = 0.02$$
$$\mathrm{P}(6, 3) = \mathrm{P}(6) \times \mathrm{P}(3) = 0.3 \times 0.1 = 0.03$$

Step 4: Sum these mutually exclusive cases:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{sum} = 9) = 0.03 + 0.02 + 0.02 + 0.03 = 0.10$$
